corrections.form_value: {"core": "unclear", "reason": "The text explicitly assigns people randomly to different generative-AI configurations for an ideation task (p. 4, Section 4). It reports 101 retained participant conversation logs, comprising 69 persona-condition and 32 control-condition participants (p. 5, Section 5), exceeding the 50-person threshold. Idea counts and semantic distances are computed on ideas extracted from their transcripts (pp. 9–10, Section 5.3). Under the requested short-screen rule, core remains unclear and the paper proceeds to the two-screener pipeline despite all three criteria being met. Design_class is other only because the RCT setting subtype is not established in the document. The stated total exclusions and the listed exclusion-category counts do not reconcile; the explicitly printed assignment and retained-sample counts are preserved without correction (p. 5, Section 5)."}
corrections.source_says: Under the supplied codebook, core should be yes: people were randomly assigned to different generative-AI configurations, the retained sample exceeds 50 people, and creativity/diversity was computed on their ideas. The paper belongs in the two-screener pipeline. An unspecified RCT setting and pending second screening do not negate these eligibility criteria; remove the reason for leaving core unclear.
corrections.quote: Random assignment allocated 73 participants to the treatment group and 32 to the control group.
corrections.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 4 (Methodology); p. 5, Section 5 (retained sample); pp. 9-10, Section 5.3 (output measures); creativity-codebook.md Sections 3 and 5; form-spec.md eligibility.core field note

corrections.source_says: Populate the exclusion field. The paper says four of 105 participants were excluded, but lists minimal interaction (n=1), inadequate session duration (n=2), session timeout violations (n=1), and content authenticity issues (n=1), which total five. Preserve this source inconsistency rather than resolving it by assumption. It separately excludes an additional three participants per group from survey analysis for incomplete responses; those survey exclusions do not define the conversation-log sample.
corrections.quote: Out of 105 participants, four were excluded due to insufficient system engagement: minimal interaction (n=1), inadequate session duration (n=2), session timeout violations (n=1), and content authenticity issues (n=1).
corrections.locator: PDF pp. 5-6, Section 5 (Results), opening paragraph; form-spec.md Counts in prose field note

corrections.source_says: The results prose reports 69 persona-condition and 32 control-condition conversation logs, but Figure 6 labels every originality comparison n=70 for treatment and n=31 for control. The total of 101 is consistent; the arm allocation is not. Retain 69/32 only as explicitly labeled prose log counts, record 70/31 as the figure labels, and add this unresolved discrepancy to open_questions. Reconciled outcome-specific arm counts are null; do not silently treat either allocation as established for every output analysis.
corrections.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 5 (Results), final-dataset sentence; p. 10, Figure 6, treatment and control labels on all three comparisons (figure inspected directly; labels are absent from extracted text)

corrections.source_says: Set paper_primary for the same-condition component of S1-O1. Figure 6 explicitly labels the same-condition originality comparison primary; the other two distances remain complementary variants. This is not evidence of preregistration.
corrections.locator: PDF p. 10, Figure 6, first x-axis label (figure inspected directly)

corrections.source_says: Populate the documented methods. S1-O1 uses cosine distances between participant portfolios represented by mean-pooled centroids of normalized OpenAI text-embedding-3-large idea embeddings: same-condition peers, all participants, and nearest cross-condition neighbor. Figure 6 labels all three tests Welch; error bars are drawn but their type and numerical bounds are not stated. S1-O2 counts ideas extracted from user transcripts with GPT-4.1. S1-O3 uses mean pairwise distance among ideas within each participant. Put complementary variants in measure_detail and the metric, embedding model, comparison sets, and Welch testing in S1-O1.diversity_detail.
corrections.quote: Three complementary originality measures were computed: (1) mean cosine distance to same-condition peers, (2) mean distance to all participants, and (3) nearest cross-condition neighbor distance.
corrections.locator: PDF pp. 9-10, Section 5.3 (Computational Creativity Assessment); p. 10, Figure 6; form-spec.md Rules 7 and diversity_detail field note

corrections.source_says: These arrays omit reported statistics. S1-O1 and S1-O3 support p_value_only: means and p-values are printed, without numerical t statistics, standard errors, or confidence intervals. S1-O2 supplies arm means and SDs but no exact test or p-value; a complete arm_means_sds_ns record needs an explicit qualification about unresolved analysis-arm Ns. Figure 6 additionally prints Welch p = 2.2e-06, p = 0.0215, and p = 0.00249 for S1-O1; its error bars have no stated type or numerical bounds. Preserve the existing prose values and do not calculate missing statistics.
corrections.quote: Idea fluency showed no significant between-condition differences, though control participants generated slightly more ideas on average (Treatment M=8.55, SD=3.85; Control M=9.23, SD=3.37).
corrections.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 5.3 (fluency); p. 10, Section 5.3 and Figure 6 (distance outcomes and plotted Welch p-values); p. 5, Section 5 (prose arm counts)

confirmed: Source version, title and author list match the PDF: arXiv:2510.26490v1 [cs.HC], 30 Oct 2025 (p. 1). The complete markdown and all 16 PDF pages were read; references occupy pp. 14-16, with no appendix or supplementary-material reference found.

One original randomized study assigned 105 undergraduate students, 73 to the persona-guided interface and 32 to baseline ChatGPT (p. 4, Section 4); this is not a synthesis, AI-versus-human-output study, or observational context study.

Randomization is explicit, but the document does not establish the location/supervision or an online-panel/coursework setting; design_class other with the form's RCT-setting explanation is defensible, and context_class none is appropriate (pp. 4-5, Section 4; p. 12, Section 6.1).

The task was generating ideas to make libraries more attractive to young adults, with 20 minutes per participant (p. 4, Section 4). Taylor used temperature 0.8 and Alex 0.3; both personas were available in treatment (p. 4), with user-initiated switching (p. 11, Section 6).

The results text explicitly reports 101 retained conversation logs, 69 persona-condition and 32 control-condition logs; those are distinct from the additional survey exclusions (pp. 5-6, Section 5). Figure 6 instead labels 70 treatment and 31 control participants (p. 10); the total still exceeds the 50-person threshold.
The output analyses use participant-level idea counts and participant-level distance summaries, rather than counting ideas, ratings, or pairs as people (pp. 9-10, Section 5.3; p. 10, Figure 6).

The participant interaction model is called baseline ChatGPT without a specific version; GPT-4.1 is explicitly named for subsequent idea extraction, and text-embedding-3-large for semantic representations (p. 4, Section 4; p. 9, Section 5.3).

S1-O1's reported prose statistics are exact: same-condition M=0.34 versus 0.28, Welch's t, p=2.20 × 10−6; all-participant M=0.33 versus 0.31, p=.02; nearest cross-condition neighbor M=0.20 versus 0.17, p<.01 (p. 10, Section 5.3). Figure 6 gives Welch p = 2.2e-06, 0.0215, and 0.00249, respectively, consistent with the prose rounding and inequality.

S1-O2's reported values are exact: Treatment M=8.55, SD=3.85; Control M=9.23, SD=3.37. The paper states no significant difference and does not give an exact p-value or test statistic for fluency (p. 9, Section 5.3).
S1-O3's reported values are exact: mean pairwise distance Treatment M=0.59, Control M=0.59, p=.90 (p. 10, Section 5.3).

Coding between-participant distances as diversity/across_people and within-participant distances as flexibility/with_ai follows the comparison sets actually described (pp. 9-10, Section 5.3; creativity-codebook.md Sections 1 and 6). The survey creativity ratings are self-reports (pp. 5-6, Table 1 and Section 5).

Every number in the one_line_finding matches the results prose: total retained sample 101 (p. 5, Section 5) and all stated outcome means and p-values (pp. 9-10, Section 5.3). Its absence of an arm breakdown does not resolve the Figure 6 count discrepancy.
summary: This randomized comparison of AI configurations assigned 105 students and retained 101, qualifying for the two-screener pipeline. Reported statistics and version match the PDF, but eligibility and missing coding fields need correction, including Figure 6's primary-outcome label and its conflicting arm counts (70/31 versus 69/32 in the text).
